newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians welcome Clinton, hope US pushes peace.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians welcome Clinton, hope US pushes peace.

text.p: Palestinians welcomed the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton and expressed hope the United States would now push stalled Middle East peace talks forward, senior PLO officials said on Wednesday.
"We consider the victory of President Clinton a positive step towards a comprehensive, just and permanent peace in the Middle East," Palestinian Legislative Council speaker Ahmed Korei told Reuters.
"It is prime time that the U.S. plays an active role in the peace talks between Palestinians and Israelis and acts as a referee," Korei said.
Senior Palestinian peace negotiator Hassan Asfour said he hoped Clinton would press Israel to implement a long-overdue troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.

"We hope his re-election will give a real push to continuing the peace process," Asfour told Reuters. "We hope that the U.S. administration will...take the necessary steps to protect peace agreements and find the right means to do so."
U.S.-sponsored Israeli-PLO talks are deadlocked over implementation of the troop pullback in Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.
Palestinians accuse Israel of trying to renegotiate the Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous centre-left government.

Israel was due to redeploy in Hebron last March. The pullback was delayed by a wave of Islamic militant attacks in Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to modify the deal to better safeguard the Jews in Hebron.
Israel's right-wing government has charged Palestinians were delaying a deal until after the American elections in the hopes of increasing U.S. pressure on the Jewish state.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday Palestinians would be disappointed if they thought he would be "whipped" by the United States after the election.
